vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: here-now
Version: 1.8.3

The 'here-now' skill is a legitimate utility for deploying static files to the here.now hosting platform. The core logic in `scripts/publish.sh` follows security best practices, such as validating the API base URL before sending Bearer tokens and using `jq` to safely handle JSON data. The instructions in `SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` describe a standard authentication and deployment workflow, including an agent-assisted sign-up process that uses one-time codes. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection; the tool's behavior is entirely consistent with its stated purpose of web publishing.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (publishes files to here.now) but there are inconsistencies and some privacy/persistence instructions (agent writing an API key to ~/.herenow and requesting email sign-in) that you should explicitly understand and approve before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description match the implementation (static hosting via here.now). However the registry metadata claims no required env vars/binaries while SKILL.md and the script require curl, file, jq and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY / ~/.herenow/credentials — this metadata mismatch is unexpected and should be corrected/confirmed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to perform network calls to here.now endpoints, run ./scripts/publish.sh, request a one-time email code, and save the returned apiKey to ~/.herenow/credentials (the SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to write the credentials file itself). The script also reads/writes a .herenow/state.json in the working directory. These actions go beyond ephemeral publishing (they persist secrets and local state) and grant the skill authority to write into the user's home directory.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) and the included publish.sh is self-contained. The script contains an error message suggesting installing jq via a curl | bash URL (https://here.now/install.sh) if jq is missing — that is an external installer URL referenced in the code and should be reviewed before running. No automatic downloads occur otherwise.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires or recommends storing an API key (HERENOW_API_KEY or ~/.herenow/credentials). The registry metadata did not declare this, creating a disparity. Requesting the user's email and instructing the agent to obtain and persist an API key in the user's home directory is a sensitive, non-trivial privilege and should be explicitly authorized by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes a per-project .herenow/state.json and encourages saving an API key to ~/.herenow/credentials. always:false and it does not modify other skills or global agent config. Persisting credentials and state is within the feature scope, but it increases the blast radius if the agent or the skill is compromised — the behavior should be clearly communicated to the user.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a legitimate static-publish workflow to here.now, but it asks the agent to perform email-based signup and to write a persistent API key into ~/.herenow/credentials and to write .herenow/state.json in the working directory. Before installing or invoking: (1) Confirm you trust the here.now service and domain (https://here.now). (2) Confirm you are comfortable with the agent writing a credential file to your home directory; if not, create and store the API key yourself and avoid agent-initiated signup. (3) Inspect scripts/publish.sh and the referenced install URL (https://here.now/install.sh) yourself before running any curl|bash commands. (4) Prefer manual key provisioning (set HERENOW_API_KEY or save credentials yourself) if you do not want the agent to persist secrets. The metadata/requirements in the registry are inconsistent with the included SKILL.md — ask the publisher to fix that discrepancy or decline installation if you need strict transparency.
